Daily GGR Trend — Aug 1–31
Dashboard Snapshotevery metric, one page

Daily Trend Aug 1–31

  • Aug 1–31: ₱26,701.25 GGR on ₱768,175 wagered (96.52% RTP).
  • Best day: Friday, Aug 28 — ₱8,677.50 GGR on ₱109,020 wagered (92.04% RTP, 9,426 rounds).
  • Weakest day: Sunday, Aug 30 — GGR dipped to −₱5,445.00 on ₱99,975 wagered, at 105.45% RTP.

Hour-of-Day rounds & GGR

  • Rounds peak in the evening (20:00–23:00, ~4,300–6,200 rounds/hr), with a secondary bump in the afternoon (14:00–15:00, ~2,900–3,600 rounds/hr) — a mobile/casual pattern outside typical office hours.
  • GGR is volatile hour-to-hour: 21:00 alone drags −₱8,380.00 despite moderate volume (4,300 rounds), while 15:00 swings sharply positive (+₱6,475.00).
  • A sign that template mix or short-run variance, not a steady house edge, is driving the hourly result.

Weekday Pattern rounds & GGR

  • Sunday is the busiest day (10,674 rounds) and also posts solid positive GGR (₱4,242.50).
  • Thursday runs high volume (8,740 rounds) but the thinnest margin (only ₱826.25 GGR) — high volume near break-even.
  • Tuesday is the only day this week with negative GGR (−₱3,488.75) despite comparable round volume (11,297) to the other weekdays.

Player Value Tiers % of bet

  • Just 8 whale players (0.82% of the base) account for 34.66% of total bet volume, and this week they are net-favored — house GGR against whales is −₱1,263.75.
  • The top 10% of players by spend account for 72.21% of total bet — revenue is concentrated in a small group.
  • If these whales churn, the impact on revenue would be significant, so they should be monitored and retained.

Bet Denomination Distribution rounds by stake

  • ₱5 is by far the most common stake (47,850 rounds, 72.93% of volume), confirming the base is dominated by micro-stakes/casual players.
  • Denominations of ₱500+ combine for 146 rounds all week (0.22% of volume), so volume is still not high-roller driven.
  • Consistent with the concentration chart: a small number of players hold an outsized bet share even though most individual rounds are tiny.

Ticket Outcome Split 79,769 rounds

  • 78.34% of rounds are a player loss, 16.47% a win, and only 5.18% a push/refund — consistent across the period.
  • New players who lose frequently right after they start tend to churn early (see Survival chart): frequent losses discourage continued play.

Bet-Type Breakdown rounds/bet/RTP, 4 categories

  • Bonus Trigger Round (betType NORMAL_BET with a nonzero otherWinAmount) is real and material: 1,492 rounds (2.27% of volume) drove a payout-heavy RTP of 1,212.37% on just ₱17,790 of bet — expected, since a triggered feature's payout isn't sized to its small base stake.
  • Buy Feature (223 rounds, 0.34%) carries a much larger average stake (₱154.71/round vs ₱10.06 for Normal Rounds) and runs a healthier RTP (79.23%) than Normal Rounds (66.94%) this week.
  • See the Math page for the full reconciled breakdown.

RTP by Template % of rounds

  • Template 4 carries the bulk of volume (45.73%) at a healthy 96.55% RTP.
  • Template 8 stands out as a house-favored outlier (75.85% RTP on 3,456 rounds).
  • Templates 7 and 9 swing player-favored (113.68% and 120.77% RTP) on smaller samples (1,923 and 1,578 rounds) — worth monitoring whether this is variance or a pattern that needs correcting.

New Player Survival % still active by round

  • Retention drops off quickly — only 58.46% of players remain active past round 20, and 30.87% past round 50.
  • Lines up with the outcome split above: 78.57% of rounds are a loss, so many players likely lose early and stop playing soon after — more an outcome/frustration effect than a technical issue.

Executive Summary

For the week of Aug 1–31, 2026, Banana Craze generated ₱768,175.00 in settled bet amount from 1,211 users across 79,769 settled rounds, landing at ₱26,701.25 GGR — a positive house result — with blended RTP at 96.52%.

  • Best day: Friday, Aug 28 — ₱8,677.50 GGR on ₱109,020 wagered (92.04% RTP).
  • Weakest day: Sunday, Aug 30 — GGR dipped to −₱5,445.00 on ₱99,975 wagered, at 105.45% RTP.
  • 948 players (78.3% of the 1,211-user base) were new to Banana Craze this period (BANANA CRAZE Only New Players).
  • 63.68% of players who reached 20 rounds were net-negative at that point.
  • Round-survival drops sharply after round 20 (58.46% retained) and again after round 50 (30.87% retained) — see the Player Analysis page for the full churn curve.

Daily Status is graded against the real production Fuse Breaker alert formula (production_fuse_monitor.py), not an invented scale — so it only escalates when the actual thing that pages the team would have fired. Checked over every rolling 12-hour window in the day (13 possible windows):
  • Warning = (small-bet winning loss ≥₱20,000 OR large-bet winning loss ≥₱60,000) AND RTP ≥102% AND 12h GGR loss ≥₱20,000.
  • Melt Candidate = the same formula with a ≥₱80,000 12h GGR loss (bet <₱200 counts as “small,” ₱200 and above is “large” — the exact BET_SPLIT constant used in production, correcting an earlier ₱15 figure that didn't match the live code).
  • Critical Review = a real ≥₱20,000 12h GGR loss occurred but RTP and/or winning-loss concentration stayed below the full formula — worth a look, not an alert.
  • Watch = benign statistical drift only (RTP outside the 90–96% band, or rounds ≥50% day-over-day) with no real GGR-loss signal.
  • Normal = none of the above.
  • None of week 36's 7 active days actually crossed the Warning or Melt gates — the worst 12h GGR loss all week was −₱5,445.00 (2026-09-01), well under the ₱20,000 Warning floor, so nothing here would have triggered a real escalation.
  • Hit Rate = rounds where payout > bet, divided by all rounds.
  • Top 5 Payout Share = the top 5 players' combined payout that day, divided by the day's total payout.
  • RTP Adjust Events = rounds where the house RTP-adjustment engine (adjustType) fired to something other than NON.
  • All figures computed directly from the settled-order cache and reconciled against the published daily/weekly totals — rounds, bet, payout and GGR match exactly for all 7 days; the 1,980-event RTP Adjust total also matches the Dynamic RTP Adjustment Mechanics breakdown on the Math & RTP page exactly.

  • 2026-09-01 has the deepest intraday drawdown of the week on both measures — its worst hour alone (09:00 PM) ran −₱8,442.50, and its worst 12-hour block (10:00 AM–10:00 PM) still runs −₱5,445.00 despite the surrounding hours partly offsetting the single-hour dip — well short of the ₱20,000 Warning / ₱80,000 Melt fuse-breaker gates (see Daily Risk & Status above).
Hour-of-Day Pattern Aug 1–31
  • Two peak windows stand out: 00:00–01:00 (4,031 + 4,114 rounds) and 20:00–23:00 (4,300–6,177 rounds, the busiest single hour of the day at 23:00).
  • The 21:00 hour is the week's single worst hour for margin at −₱8,380.00 GGR despite heavy volume (4,300 rounds) — a 106.09% hourly RTP outlier worth a template-mix check.
  • Early hours also swing: 00:00 spikes to +₱2,152.50 GGR while 06:00 dips to −₱143.75.

  • Bonus Trigger Round is real and material — 1,492 rounds (2.27% of volume) triggered a nonzero "other payout" on top of the base bet, contributing ₱215,680.00 of payout from only ₱17,790.00 of bet in those rounds.
  • That payout-to-bet ratio (1,212.37%) is expected, not an error: a Bonus Trigger Round's payout is driven by the feature outcome, not by the small base stake that triggered it, so per-category RTP is not comparable to the blended RTP.
  • Buy Feature rounds (223, 0.34%) carry a much larger average stake (₱154.71/round vs ₱10.06 for Normal Rounds) and actually run a healthier RTP (79.23%) than Normal Rounds (66.94%) this week.
  • Feature reconciliation: Normal Rounds (63,900) + Bonus Trigger Round (1,492) + Mission Feature (0) + Buy Feature (223) = 79,769 settled rounds. Total settled rounds = 79,769. Result: PASSED.

Unlike the monthly report's version of this panel — pulled live from queryPageRtpAdjustRecord — this week's numbers come straight from the adjustType field already present on every settled order row, so no separate live pull was needed to reconstruct the type breakdown and reach figures. Only the two trigger-threshold configuration values above genuinely require that live endpoint and aren't available for this week.
  • DAILY and CUMULATIVE dominate (82.72% of all 1,980 events) and both run RTP well above 300%: these are compensation events that push payout up once the rolling RTP drifts below a trigger threshold, and they're the same underlying mechanic behind the Bonus Trigger Round RTP outlier (1,212.37%) already flagged in the panel above.
  • DISCARD and REROLL events run close to or below 100% RTP and read as adjustments that were calculated but not fully paid out.
  • Adjust events touch only 2.17% of the week's bet volume but 5.97% of its payout — a small, engineered slice of rounds doing disproportionate work to hold the blended RTP near target — and 66.2% of the week's players hit at least one of them.
